verses.text: Di proverbs of Solomon, di son of David, king of Israel,
to know wisdom and instruction, to understand words of understanding,
to receive instruction for wise dealing, for righteousness, justice and fairness,
to give prudence to di simple, knowledge and discretion to di young man.
Make di wise man hear and increase learning. Make di man of understanding get wise counsel,
to understand proverb and parable, di words of di wise and dem riddles.
Di fear of di Lord na di beginning of knowledge, but fools despise wisdom and instruction.
My pikin, hear di instruction of your papa, and no forsake di teaching of your mama,
because dem na garland of grace for your head and chains for your neck.
My pikin, if sinners entice you, no gree.
If dem talk say, “Come with us. Make we lie in wait for blood. Make we ambush di innocent without cause.
Make we swallow dem alive like Sheol, and whole, like dem wey go down into di pit.
We go find all kinds of precious wealth. We go fill our houses with plunder.
Cast your lot among us. Make we all share one purse.”
My pikin, no waka for di way with dem. Hold back your foot from dem path,
because dem feet dey run to evil, and dem dey hurry to shed blood.
Surely for vain dem dey spread di net for di sight of any bird,
but dem lie in wait for dem own blood. Dem ambush dem own lives.
So na di ways of everyone wey dey greedy for gain. E dey take away di life of im owners.
Wisdom dey cry aloud for di street. E dey raise im voice for di public squares.
E dey call for di head of di noisy crowds. For di entrance of di gates, for di city e dey speak im words:
“How long, una simple ones, una go love simplicity? How long una scoffers go delight for scoffing, and fools hate knowledge?
Turn to my reproof. Look, I go pour out my spirit on una. I go make my words known to una.
Because I don call, and una refuse. I don stretch out my hand, and nobody pay attention,
but una don ignore all my counsel and no accept my reproof.
I go laugh for una calamity. I go mock when di fear of una come,
when di fear of una come like storm, and una calamity come like whirlwind, when distress and anguish come on una.
Den dem go call on me, but I no go answer. Dem go seek me diligently, but dem no go find me,
because dem hate knowledge and no choose di fear of di Lord.
Dem no accept my counsel. Dem despise all my reproof.
So dem go eat di fruit of dem own way and dey filled with dem own schemes.
Because di turning away of di simple go kill dem, and di complacency of fools go destroy dem.
But whoever listen to me go dwell securely and go dey quiet, without fear of evil.”
My pikin, if you go receive my words and store up my commandments within you,
so dat you make your ear attentive to wisdom and turn your heart to understanding,
yes, if you cry out for discernment and lift up your voice for understanding,
if you seek am like silver and search for am like hidden treasures,
den you go understand di fear of di Lord and find di knowledge of God.
Because di Lord dey give wisdom. Out of im mouth dey come knowledge and understanding.
E dey store up sound wisdom for di upright. E be shield to dem wey waka for integrity,
to guard di paths of justice and watch over di way of im holy ones.
Den you go understand righteousness and justice, fairness and every good path.
Because wisdom go enter your heart, and knowledge go dey pleasant to your soul.
Discretion go watch over you. Understanding go keep you,
to deliver you from di way of evil, from di man wey speak perverse things,
wey leave di paths of uprightness to waka for di ways of darkness,
wey rejoice to do evil and delight for di perverseness of evil,
whose paths dey crooked, and wey dey devious for dem ways.
To deliver you from di woman wey no be your own, from di foreigner wey dey flatter with im words,
wey forsake di partner of im youth and forget di covenant of im God.
Because im house dey sink down to death and im paths to di dead.
None wey go to am return again, and dem no reach di paths of life.
So you go waka for di way of good men and keep di paths of di righteous.
Because di upright go dwell for di land, and di perfect go remain inside am.
But di wicked go cut off from di land, and di treacherous go dey rooted out of am.
My pikin, no forget my teaching, but make your heart keep my commandments,
because dem go add long days and years of life and peace to you.
No let love and faithfulness forsake you. Bind dem around your neck. Write dem on di tablet of your heart.
So you go find favor and good understanding for di sight of God and man.
Trust for di Lord with all your heart, and no lean on your own understanding.
For all your ways acknowledge am, and e go make your paths straight.
No dey wise for your own eyes. Fear di Lord and turn away from evil.
E go be health to your body and nourishment to your bones.
Honor di Lord with your wealth and with di first fruits of all your increase,
so dat your barns go dey filled with plenty, and your vats go overflow with new wine.
My pikin, no despise di discipline of di Lord, and no hate im reproof,
because di Lord dey reprove di one wey e love, as papa di pikin wey e delight for.
Blessed na di man wey find wisdom, di man wey get understanding,
because di profit from am better pass profit from silver, and di gain from am pass fine gold.
E precious pass rubies. Nothing wey you fit desire fit compare with am.
Long life dey for im right hand. For im left hand na riches and honor.
Im ways na ways of pleasantness, and all im paths na peace.
E be tree of life to dem wey lay hold of am. Everyone wey hold am fast dey blessed.
Di Lord by wisdom found di earth. By understanding e establish di heavens.
By im knowledge di depths break open, and di skies drop di dew.
My pikin, no let dem depart from your eyes. Keep sound wisdom and discretion,
and dem go be life to your soul and grace to your neck.
Den you go waka for your way securely, and your foot no go stumble.
When you lie down, you no go dey afraid. Yes, you go lie down, and your sleep go sweet.
No dey afraid of sudden terror, nor of di ruin of di wicked when e come,
because di Lord go be your confidence and go keep your foot from being caught.
No withhold good from dem wey e belong to, when e dey for di power of your hand to do am.
No talk to your neighbor say, “Go, and come back, and tomorrow I go give,” when you get am with you.
No plan evil against your neighbor, wey dey dwell securely near you.
No quarrel with man without cause, if e no do you harm.
No envy di man of violence, and no choose any of im ways.
Because di devious dey abomination to di Lord, but im friendship dey with di upright.
Di curse of di Lord dey for di house of di wicked, but e dey bless di dwelling of di righteous.
Toward di scoffers e dey scoff, but to di humble e dey give grace.
Di wise go inherit honor, but fools dey carry shame.
Hear, una pikin dem, di instruction of one papa, and pay attention to know understanding,
because I give you good teaching. No forsake my law.
Because I be pikin to my papa, tender and only one for di sight of my mama.
E teach me, and e talk to me say, “Make your heart hold my words. Keep my commandments, and live.
Get wisdom. Get understanding. No forget, and no turn away from di words of my mouth.
No forsake am, and e go keep you. Love am, and e go watch over you.
Di beginning of wisdom na dis: get wisdom. Yes, with all your getting get understanding.
Esteem am, and e go exalt you. E go bring you honor, when you embrace am.
E go give to your head garland of grace. E go deliver to you crown of splendor.”
Hear, my pikin, and receive my sayings, and di years of your life go be many.
I don teach you di way of wisdom. I don lead you for straight paths.
When you waka, your steps no go dey hampered, and when you run, you no go stumble.
Take hold of instruction. No let go. Keep am, because na your life.
No enter di path of di wicked, and no waka for di way of evil men.
Avoid am. No pass by am. Turn away from am and pass on.
Because dem no fit sleep unless dem don do evil, and dem sleep go fly from dem unless dem don make person stumble.
Because dem dey eat bread of wickedness and drink wine of violence.
But di path of di righteous na like di light of dawn, wey dey shine brighter and brighter until di full day.
Di way of di wicked na like darkness. Dem no know wetin dem dey stumble over.
My pikin, pay attention to my words. Bend your ear to my sayings.
No let dem depart from your eyes. Keep dem inside your heart,
because dem na life to dem wey find dem and health to all dem flesh.
Keep your heart with all diligence, because out of am na di wellsprings of life.
Put away from you crooked speech and put devious talk far from you.
Make your eyes look straight ahead, and make your gaze dey fixed straight before you.
Consider di path of your feet, and make all your ways dey established.
No turn to di right hand or to di left. Turn your foot away from evil.
My pikin, pay attention to my wisdom. Bend your ear to my understanding,
so dat you go keep discretion, and your lips go guard knowledge.
Because di lips of foreign woman drip honey, and im mouth smoother pass oil,
but for di end e bitter like wormwood, sharp like two edged sword.
Im feet go down to death. Im steps lay hold of Sheol.
E no consider di path of life. Im ways wander, and e no know am.
Now, una pikin dem, listen to me, and no depart from di words of my mouth.
Keep your way far from am. No come near di door of im house,
so dat you no go give your honor to others, and your years to di cruel,
and strangers no go take your wealth, and your labor no go dey inside another man house,
and you go groan at di end, when your flesh and your body don waste away,
and talk say, “How I don hate instruction, and my heart despise reproof!
I no obey di voice of my teachers, nor bend my ear to dem wey teach me!
I almost come to total ruin, for di middle of di assembly and congregation.”
Drink water from your own well and running water from your own spring.
Make your springs overflow outside, streams of water for di streets.
Make dem be for you alone, and no for strangers with you.
Make your fountain dey blessed. Rejoice with di wife of your youth,
loving doe and graceful deer. Make im breasts satisfy you at all times. Always dey intoxicated with im love.
Why, my pikin, you go dey intoxicated with foreign woman and embrace di bosom of stranger?
Because di ways of man dey before di eyes of di Lord, and e ponder all im paths.
Di iniquities of di wicked man go catch am, and e go dey held with di cords of im sin.
E go die for lack of instruction. For di greatness of im folly e go go astray.
My pikin, if you don become guarantor for your neighbor, if you don shake hands for stranger,
if you don dey trapped by di words of your mouth, you don dey caught by di words of your mouth,
do dis now, my pikin, and deliver yourself, since you don fall into di hand of your neighbor: go, humble yourself, and press your plea with your neighbor.
Give no sleep to your eyes, nor slumber to your eyelids.
Deliver yourself like gazelle from di hand of di hunter, like bird from di hand of di fowler.
Go to di ant, you lazy one. Consider im ways and be wise,
wey no get chief, overseer or ruler,
yet e dey prepare im food for di summer and gather im provision for harvest.
How long you go lie down, you lazy one? When you go rise from your sleep?
Small sleep, small slumber, small folding of di hands to rest,
so your poverty go come like robber, and your want like armed man.
Worthless person, wicked man, dey waka with perverse mouth,
e dey wink with im eyes, e dey speak with im feet, e dey point with im fingers.
Perverseness dey im heart. E dey plot evil continually. E dey sow discord.
Therefore im calamity go come suddenly. Sudden e go break, and no remedy go dey.
Dis six things di Lord hate. Yes, seven na abomination to am:
proud eyes, lying tongue, hands wey shed innocent blood,
heart wey plan wicked schemes, feet wey hurry to run to evil,
false witness wey breathe out lies, and person wey sow discord among brothers.
My pikin, keep your papa commandment, and no forsake your mama teaching.
Bind dem continually on your heart. Tie dem around your neck.
When you waka, e go lead you. When you sleep, e go watch over you. When you wake, e go talk with you.
Because di commandment na lamp, and di teaching na light. Di reproofs of instruction na di way of life,
to keep you from di evil woman, from di flattering tongue of di foreign woman.
No lust after im beauty for your heart, and no let am capture you with im eyelids.
Because for price of prostitute, man dey reduced to loaf of bread, but di adulteress dey hunt di precious life.
Man fit carry fire for im lap, and im clothes no go burn?
Or one fit waka on hot coals, and im feet no go dey scorched?
So na di one wey go sleep with im neighbor wife. Whoever touch am no go go unpunished.
Men no dey despise thief if e steal to satisfy im appetite when e dey hungry,
but if e dey found, e must pay back seven times. E must give all di wealth of im house.
Whoever commit adultery with woman lack sense. E wey do am dey destroy im own soul.
E go get wounds and dishonor, and im disgrace no go dey wiped away.
Because jealousy dey make man furious, and e no go spare for di day of vengeance.
E no go accept any ransom, nor rest content though you multiply gifts.
My pikin, keep my words and store up my commandments with you.
Keep my commandments and live, and my teaching as di apple of your eye.
Bind dem on your fingers. Write dem on di tablet of your heart.
Talk to wisdom say, “You be my sister,” and call understanding your relative,
so dat dem go keep you from di foreign woman, from di adulteress wey flatter with im words.
Because for di window of my house I look through my lattice,
and I see among di simple ones, I perceive among di young men, one young man wey lack sense,
passing through di street near im corner, going along di way to im house,
for di twilight, for di evening of di day, for di middle of night and darkness.
Look, woman meet am, dressed as prostitute and cunning of heart.
E loud and stubborn. Im feet no dey stay for house.
Now for di streets, now for di squares, and dey lie in wait for every corner.
So e catch am and kiss am, and with bold face e talk to am say,
“I get peace offerings. Today I don pay my vows.
So I come out to meet you, to seek your face diligently, and I don find you.
I don spread my bed with coverings, with colored linen from Egypt.
I don perfume my bed with myrrh, aloes and cinnamon.
Come, make we take our fill of love until morning. Make we enjoy love.
Because my husband no dey home. E don go on long journey.
E don take bag of money with am. E go come home for di full moon.”
With much persuasion e cause am to yield. With flattering lips e force am.
Sudden e follow am, as ox go to di slaughter, or as fool to di discipline of di stocks,
until arrow pierce im liver, as bird hurry to di snare and no know say e go cost im life.
Now, una pikin dem, listen to me. Pay attention to di words of my mouth.
No let your heart turn aside to im ways. No stray for im paths,
because e don bring down many wounded. Yes, all im slain na mighty multitude.
Im house na di way to Sheol, going down to di rooms of death.
Wisdom no dey cry out? Understanding no dey raise im voice?
For di top of di heights beside di way, where di paths meet, e stand.
Beside di gates, for di entrance of di town, for di doors, e cry aloud:
“To you, men, I call, and my voice dey to di sons of man.
Una simple ones, understand prudence. Una fools, get understanding heart.
Listen, because I go speak excellent things, and di opening of my lips go be right things.
Because my mouth go speak truth, and wickedness na abomination to my lips.
All di words of my mouth dey righteous. Nothing twisted or crooked dey inside dem.
Dem all dey plain to di one wey understand, and right to dem wey find knowledge.
Receive my instruction instead of silver, and knowledge rather than choice gold.
Because wisdom better pass rubies. All wey you fit desire no fit compare with am.
I, wisdom, dwell with prudence, and I find knowledge and discretion.
Di fear of di Lord na to hate evil. Pride, arrogance, di evil way and perverse mouth I hate.
Counsel and sound wisdom na my own. I be understanding. Power na my own.
By me kings reign, and rulers decree justice.
By me princes rule, and nobles, all di judges of di earth.
I love dem wey love me. Dem wey seek me diligently go find me.
Riches and honor dey with me, enduring wealth and righteousness.
My fruit better pass gold, yes, fine gold, and my yield pass choice silver.
I waka for di way of righteousness, for di paths of justice,
to cause dem wey love me to inherit wealth. I go fill dem treasuries.
Di Lord get me for di beginning of im work, before im deeds of old.
From everlasting dem set me up, from di beginning, before di earth.
When no depths dey, dem bring me forth, when no springs dey wey dey full of water.
Before dem set di mountains, before di hills, dem bring me forth,
before e don make di earth and di fields, or di first dust of di world.
When e establish di heavens, I dey dere. When e set circle on di surface of di deep,
when e make firm di skies above, when di springs of di deep dey established,
when e give di sea im boundary, so dat di waters no go disobey im command, when e mark out di foundations of di earth,
den I dey beside am as master workman. I dey im delight every day, dey rejoice always before am,
dey rejoice for im inhabited world, and my delight dey among di pikin dem of men.
Now, una pikin dem, listen to me, because blessed na dem wey keep my ways.
Hear instruction and be wise, and no refuse am.
Blessed na di man wey listen to me, wey dey watch daily for my gates, wey dey wait beside my doorposts.
Because whoever find me find life and obtain favor from di Lord.
But di one wey miss me wrong im own soul. All dem wey hate me love death.”
